purpose.summary: Use captured immutable native ancestors for service startup instead of cloning the complete native block index; preserve strict owned fixtures and all runtime limits.
scope: Direct child of signed public main 2fd87f2 integrated by PR63; eight technical postimages plus finite source policy, documentation and CI.
Capture only the native tip and chain/pool generations, under both native locks, with allocation before locking.
Use the captured branch for height/fork lookup during unchanged upstream Chronik resync, then seed the retained suffix and reconcile before admission.
Pin the native header/storage writer and joined teardown contracts; retain per-read block/undo storage fencing.
Retain all 62 inherited archival native case bodies and add six cases with 74 assertions under the existing fixed deadlines.
exclusions: No mainnet admission, runtime limit/default change, continuous-ingress liveness or operator-plugin claim.
No upstream indexer, ALP/token algorithm, plugin engine, dependency, consensus, network identity, RPC or wallet change.
No incoming reports, private history, operator material, server access, deployment, cutover, release, desktop integration or automatic proof promotion.

commands: Build the exact public compiled-out profile with unchanged native prerequisites.
expected_results: The standalone node builds without Chronik linkage and retains all inherited controls.

commands: Build the exact public regtest-plugins profile with existing locked Rust inputs and unchanged native prerequisites.
expected_results: The daemon and native fixture build; inherited profiles retain their existing boundaries.

scenarios.command: Run the native-startup six-case group, the unchanged owned-startup and startup-metadata-batches groups, and every inherited profile-bound group in fresh processes.
expected_results: Six cases and 74 assertions pass: no owned graph, stable references across rehash, captured branch across progress/reorg, refused read-time storage drift, cancellation and foreign-owner guards, real upstream offline rewind/reopen.
All 62 inherited archival case bodies and every existing daemon/ALP/plugin client and fixed deadline remain unchanged.
failure_conditions: Wrong case/assertion count, an owned graph in service startup, fork lookup following the wrong branch, stale storage read accepted, incomplete startup publication, source/build drift, timeout, skip, nonzero exit or cleanup failure.

limitations: Constant-size capture does not bound upstream database/index memory, disk resources or total historical resync duration.
Native immutable header/ancestor fields and unpruned non-relocating storage require the pinned source/lifetime contract; const pointers alone do not own native resources.
No live index unload/reload, header replacement, pruning or storage relocation is supported while a service borrower exists.
There is no all-history copied-position comparison at service finish; a late unsupported mutation after an earlier read is not claimed to be detected by a global final scan.
Strict owned historical fixtures retain their exact atomic final storage fence and remain separate controls.
Runtime remains unpruned local regtest, maximum height 2000, indexes/mempool 4096, with retained payload/reorganization budgets.
System build dependencies remain unlocked; no reproducible-build, full-history, continuous-ingress, operator-plugin or mainnet-readiness claim.
counterevidence: Historical startup and aggregate stop/reopen timeouts and upstream dependency alerts remain open.
No server, operator datadir, mainnet history or production replacement is exercised.
